table.title: Net Value of the Foreign Trade of China, 1915 to 1924
footnotes: * Net Imports, i.e. the value of the Foreign Goods imported direct from Foreign Countries less the value of the Foreign Goods re-exported to Foreign Countries during the year.

The values given in the above tables do not include the value of goods carried coastwise, nor do they comprise the whole extent of the Foreign Trade, inasmuch as vessels of Chinese type, which are not within the control of the Maritime Customs, ply between Foreign and Chinese (both Treaty and non-Treaty) Ports.

table.title: Marine Department

rows: Hainan coast: Waichow Island to Hailingshan.

The West River from Samchow to the sea, with the Gaemoon, the Fotomoon, and the Motomoon; the Kumchuk Creek; the Wangmoon approach to the West River, including Mahning Reach, Junction Channel, and Kerr Channel; and the creek to the southward of the Wangmoon approach.
The West River from Cock's Comb to Samchow and the Fatshan branch as far as its junction with the Shuntak branch.
West River from Wuchow to Cock's Comb.
Hangchow Bay to the old mouth of the Yellow River (34° N. lat.) and up the Yangtze to Vine Point.
The Yangtze from Vine Point to the Icheng Rocks from Vine Point to Nanking.
The Yangtze from the Icheng Rocks to the Rosina Rock.
The Yangtze from the Rosina Rock to Anking, and from Nanking to Tatung.
Includes the Yangtze River from Anking to where the Matsushan touches the river below Wusueh and from Tatung to where the Matsushan touches the river below Wusueh.

The Yangtze River from where the Matsushan touches the river to Yochow. For matters affecting the Marine Department, the upper limit of the Hankow District is Hankow. The Hankow office is the headquarters for the Lower and Middle Yangtze administration.

The Yangtze River from Hankow to Low Point and the waterways comprising the Yochow—Changteh—Tsingshih routes, whether across the Tungting Lake or via the lower part of the Siang River, up to Lolintan. The Yochow office controls all aids on the Changsha, Changteh, and Ichang routes.
The Yangtze River from Low Point to Tungshih, and from Tsingshih to Sungtzekow and Taiping-kow.
The Yangtze River from Tungshih to the Szechwan-Hupeh boundary.
The Yangtze River from the Szechwan-Hupeh boundary to the boundary of Tibet.
From the old mouth of the Yellow River to the Tatsinho.
